items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to emergency intervention for persons impaired by alcohol or other substances
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6248

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to emergency
intervention for persons impaired by alcohol or other substances

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

This legislation seeks to create a robust involuntary alcohol or
substance abuse treatment procedure for individuals who are a danger
to themselves and others as a result of their systematic abuse of
alcohol or drugs.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill sets forth and amends definitions used in this
article. This section allows for voluntary emergency services by
requiring law enforcement to transport an individual who consents, to
a facility that provides emergency services. This section also allows
for a person who appears to be incapacitated by alcohol and or
substance to the degree that there is a likelihood of harm to the
person or others shall be taken to a treatment facility for the
purposes of receiving emergency services. A person who comes
voluntarily shall be provided emergency services at such place if
found suitable or referred to another suitable facility or treatment
program, or sent home. A person who is brought in with objection shall
be examined by a physician as soon as possible, if such physician
determines such person is incapacitated by alcohol and/or substance to
the degree that there is a likelihood to result in harm that
individual may be retained for emergency treatment to achieve
stabilization. This section also extends the hold time an individual
may be held from 48 hours to 72 hours.

Subdivision (c) of this section allows for the director of a treatment
facility to provide involuntary emergency services upon the
certificate of a local director of community services or a physician
when in their opinion the individual is incapacitated in such a way
that their use of alcohol or substance is likely to result in harm to
himself, herself or others. The need for immediate involuntary
emergency services shall be confirmed prior to admission by a
physician affiliated with the facility.  Excluding Sundays and
holidays if it is recommended that the individual remain beyond
seventy-two hours and the patient does not agree, the certificate of
such physician attesting that the patient is in need shall be filed
with the facility. From the time of the patient's admission the
retention of an individual beyond seventy-two hours shall be subject
to notice, hearing, review, and judicial approval.

Subdivision (d) allows a petition for emergency services to be sought
for an adult or for a minor by petition to a local government unit's
director of community services and further allows to designate those
who may petition. States that a petition for admission shall be based
upon a personal examination that must establish the reason for
admission as to belief as to why the individual is a likelihood to
result in harm to themselves or others. Each person admitted shall be
provided with written notice regarding patient rights, have access to
their personal attorney upon request and notice as to the availability
of the mental hygiene legal service for legal counsel. The
Commissioner shall promulgate regulations for taking individuals to
their residence or to appropriate public or private treatment
facilities and minimizing the role of police in obtaining treatment
for such persons.

Section 2 adds a new section 22.13 of the mental hygiene law related
to court authorization to retain an involuntary patient.If a person is
in need of retention beyond seventy-two hours and if such patient does
not agree to remain in such facility, the director shall apply to the
supreme court of the county court for an order authorizing continued
retention. The facility is authorized to retain the patient for
seventy-two hours or during the period which the application may be
pending not to exceed ninety days. Written notice shall be given to
the patient as well as mental hygiene legal services. Notice shall
state that a hearing may be requested by the patient within five days.

Section 3 Allows for involuntary admission procedures for minors. No
minor shall be able to discharge themselves prior to the seventy-two
hour hold time. A copy of their patient's rights shall be given and
explained to the minor, and to the minor's consenting parent or
guardian. The minor shall be required to sign a form indicating that
he or she has been advised of their ability to access mental hygiene
legal services. Further this section makes changes to discharge
procedures allowing that the minor's parent or guardian consents to
the release of the minor.

Section 4 is the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

As we face an ever growing heroin problem, new laws are needed to help
get individuals with addiction problems help. This legislation goes
beyond heroin to cover alcohol and other substances as well. However,
let it not be lost that countless families throughout New York are
looking for ways to get their loved ones help. Every option needs to
be explored to get individuals into treatment. For example an
individual who is revived using Nalaxone. A report by the National
Institute on Drug Abuse titled Principles of Drug Addiction Treatment:
A Research-Based Guide argues that treatment does not need to be
voluntary to be effective.  Specifically they state that "Sanctions or
enticements from family, employment settings, and/or the criminal
justice system can significantly increase treatment entry, retention
rates, and the ultimate success of drug treatment interventions." This
legislation allows for an individual to be held for up to 72 hours for
detoxification as opposed to the current 48 hours. Beyond this the
legislation takes important new steps to allow for an individual to be
involuntarily committed for up to 90 days if they are found to be a
danger to themselves and or others.It cannot be argued that an
individual who has died and been brought back to life using Nalaxone
should be considered a danger to themselves and this legislation would
enable them to receive the treatment they deserve.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New Bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

To be determined

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
